entries.notes: RETIRED 2026-08-05 — BAKEOFF LOST. Every candidate came back as a sculpted HUMAN FACE (nose, lips, cheekbones), mostly face-on, not as a mask object. ROOT CAUSE, and it is the opposite of the round-11 diagnosis in players.json: that note says a blank oval carries no facing information, so this prompt was given a landmark budget (brow ridge, mouth aperture, eye sockets) to break the oval — but those landmarks ARE face anatomy, so the model drew a face. A mask has to be specified as an ABSENCE of face (smooth featureless fired plate, no nose, no lips, no cheekbones, with all of those as hard negatives) and given its front through LIGHTING and RIM GEOMETRY instead. Untested; this is the arm to run if masks are ever revisited.

entries.notes: RETIRED 2026-08-05 — BAKEOFF LOST, WORST ARM. Chaining from sprites/classes/summoner.png at strength 45 imported the FIGURE, not the mask: candidate 2 came back as a woman with long red hair (the deep-red robe became hair), the others got a cowl and a headwrap. GENERAL RULE LEARNED: the players.json advice 'chain from whichever accepted sibling already has the property you keep failing to get' only holds when the property is the SUBJECT of the source image. Here the mask is a small feature on a robed body, so the chain asserts the body. This is not fixable by lowering strength — it is the wrong anchor. A mask chain would need a source image whose subject is a mask.

Removing ALL facial landmarks (the fix for round 1's face problem) produced smooth featureless eggs/pebbles with two teal gems: no facing, no character.
